overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Selection Panel properly held its December 7, 2011 preliminary screening of superintendent search applicants in executive session under Purpose 8.

allegations.summary: Complaint that a three-member selection panel's December 7, 2011 executive session to screen superintendent search committee applicants did not qualify under Purpose 8.
allegations.key_passage: We find this reason to be sufficient justification for a preliminary screening committee to conduct its preliminary screening process in executive session under Purpose 8.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the panel could not claim open discussion would deter applicants because it did not tell applicants before the deadline that screening would be private.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Search Panel did include a notice assuring some level of confidentiality in the review process

allegations.summary: Complaint that because all 33 applicants were forwarded to the full committee for open discussion, the panel could not claim applicants would object to public discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Although all 33 candidates were ultimately considered by the Committee in open session, it was not unreasonable for the Search Panel to believe that the candidates might not be willing to have their qualifications reviewed openly during the initial stage of the process.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
